title: Lots of new AutoSprite updates this week, including isometric mode that turns one image into a full spritesheet that you can play and test instantly
author: beelllllll
selftext:
I wanted to share another quick update as I’ve been heads down building nonstop since my last post.

I’m the creator of AutoSprite. It’s a platform that takes a single image and turns it into full, playable sets of spritesheets (idle, walk, run, jump, attack and custom actions, etc). After you pick your animations you can test your spritesheets right in the browser.

I originally made this because I always wanted something like it when I was making games: drop in an image and get animations that actually work in a game.

Over the last month I’ve been improving a ton of stuff, but the biggest thing I’ve been obsessed with is perfect loops. I’ve been narrowing in on making all animations and loops feel smooth out of the box.

New since the last post:
* Isometric mode just launched today! You can  now generate isometric spritesheets from a single image
* Auto detect the best loop start end frames
* Much more mobile friendly!
* More robust system, less errors, quicker generations
* New Stream Avatars export format 

Still early, lots to improve, but I’m trying to make it better every day.

https://www.autosprite.io/

Always happy to hear feedback or new ideas, thank you!

comments.author: alexmtl

replies.author: beelllllll
replies.body:
Currently it has a bit of trouble with non humanoid but it gets it right sometimes. I’m working on a fix to work with humanoid and non humanoid .

You can get really far with the “custom” animation and tuning off the prompt helper so it truly fits your needs, just make sure you have a very detailed prompt

replies.author: beelllllll
replies.body: Sorry, current I only have Google account registration, in the future I can add normal email registration. I’ll put it on the todo list, thanks for the feedback!

replies.author: IncorrectAddress
replies.body: That won't matter to me, I'm not going to register my email to something just to try it out, you need something that bridges that gap for potential users to test the product.

replies.author: RikerRiker
replies.body: Agreed. I'm in marketing myself. I'd suggest you let a visitor create something right on your homepage or landing page to see it in action. Then to download or edit, they need to sign up. Make the user get enticed without friction of signing up.
